Commercial vehicle finance

After this lesson you can:
  • Underwrite the vehicle as a business
  • Bring permits and route economics into credit

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

1. The product

Finance for trucks, buses and fleet vehicles where the vehicle earns its own EMI. Underwriting therefore models route economics — permit type, route or use code, fleet experience, projected vehicle cash flows — on top of the dealer/registration/insurance machinery of the personal vehicle journey.

The borrower ranges from a first-time single-truck operator to a fleet company, and policy differentiates sharply: fleet size and operator vintage are contract facts, not colour.

2. What a BA watches

Permit tracking is the journey's special servicing duty — an expired national/state permit idles the asset and its cash flow. Vehicle cash-flow review continues through the loan; commercial vehicles are also where repossession (module 6) is most operationally real, with yard, inventory and release controls.

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. Why is the permit a servicing-time concern, not just an origination check?

  1. Permits never expire
  2. An expired permit idles the vehicle — killing the very cash flow that services the loan
  3. RTO requires it
  4. Insurance depends on it
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. The asset's earning licence is the repayment source; the contract tracks it for the life of the loan.
